title: Security testing — requirements and the tests that verify them
note:
Each requirement names the golden tests that verify it, and traceability.mjs checks this file against what actually ran: a requirement with no test, a test id that does not exist, and a named test that did not pass are all failures.

Two requirements are deliberately not on this list because nothing here verifies them, and adding a row that points at no evidence would be worse than the gap. Detection against an application AIRA has not seen is not measurable in a lab whose flaws were written alongside the checks (SECN-003). Browser-driven DOM XSS is not implemented (SECN-002). Both are recorded as NOT VERIFIED in the golden results rather than omitted.

SEC-R43 to SEC-R49 are about AIRA itself rather than the applications it tests. A security testing tool that is not itself secure is a liability, and its own tenancy, credential handling and target policy are verified by the same kind of test as everything else here.

requirements.statement: Security testing runs only against an application somebody has explicitly authorized in writing.
Security scope is never unrestricted: an empty allowlist permits nothing and an unlisted host is refused.
Arbitrary URLs are never testable, and cloud metadata and link-local addresses are refused whatever the scope says.
A security check cannot bypass the scope guard; the declared risk can be raised by the HTTP verb and never lowered.
Destructive testing is off by default and needs both a scope that permits it and a caller who may run it.
Security scanning never performs a load or denial-of-service test; every volume probe is bounded and says so.
Production security testing is disabled by default and refused unless authorized for that run.
The security lab uses only synthetic identities and synthetic data; no real credential is used anywhere.
Secrets never appear in the evidence a report links to, and redaction does not destroy the evidence.
No vulnerability is reported without a reproducible request/response exchange behind it.
A finding's severity is computed from stored factors and is reproducible, never assigned by a model.
Broken object level authorization is detected, with a control proving the owner can read what the intruder cannot.
Broken function level authorization and privilege escalation are detected.
Missing authorization and unverified tokens are detected.
Authentication weaknesses are detected: user enumeration, missing lockout, session survival after sign-out, excessive session lifetime and reset-token reuse.
API security flaws are detected: mass assignment, missing input validation, unsafe methods, missing rate limiting and excessive data exposure.
Reflected and stored XSS are detected, and reflection alone is never reported as XSS.
SQL, NoSQL, command and template injection are detected by indicator, with nothing extracted or executed.
CSRF and missing origin validation are detected, with a control that the legitimate request succeeds.
File upload restrictions are tested without uploading anything executable, and path traversal in a filename is detected.
Open redirect is detected by reading the Location header and never by following it.
SSRF is detected without probing cloud metadata by default.
Passive checks detect missing security headers, insecure cookie attributes, dangerous CORS, directory listings, exposed source maps and verbose errors.
A permissive CORS policy without credentials is not reported as a vulnerability.
Every detector is silent against the corrected application; false positives are measured, not assumed.
Endpoints that behave correctly produce no finding even while the rest of the application is vulnerable.
Scan profiles bound what a scan will do, and each profile refuses the risk levels above it.
What a scan was refused is recorded, so coverage can be read from what it did not do.
Areas a scan cannot decide are reported as untested, never as clean.
A build with no security scan is never reported as passing a security gate.
A partial scan does not pass a security gate however clean its findings were.
New findings at or above the configured severity block a build; the gate can also pass.
A security regression fails the gate at any severity.
A suppressed finding with no written justification and no named decision-maker is counted as open.
A finding's status history is appended to, never overwritten, so the decisions form an audit trail.
A false positive suppresses one finding and never the same class elsewhere.
Nothing automated can mark a security finding resolved or suppressed; self-healing cannot hide a regression.
A finding absent from a scan is never recorded as fixed on absence alone.
Findings have a stable identity across runs that survives rewording and severity revision.
No report claims an application is secure or that it has zero vulnerabilities.
A low-confidence finding goes to review rather than stopping a release.
Security scanning, triage and authorization are permission-gated in the API and in the console, and none is available to a read-only user.
AIRA's own API refuses unauthenticated and forged-token requests on every data endpoint.
AIRA isolates tenants: one organization cannot read or act inside another's data by knowing an identifier.
AIRA stores injection payloads as data and never executes them.
AIRA refuses to point its own crawler or scanner at targets that are never legitimate.
Credentials AIRA stores for an application under test are never returned by its API.
AIRA's own artifact paths cannot be turned into a traversal, and arbitrary script execution needs an explicit opt-in.
AIRA sets the browser security headers it claims to.
The security controls permit an authorized scan as well as refusing an unauthorized one; they are not a refusal of everything.
A security scope is stored with the written authorization, the person who gave it and when, and cannot be enabled without one.
Destructive testing and production can never be authorized together, refused where somebody configures it rather than one request at a time.
A scan cannot be recorded against an application with no enabled scope, and a finding with no evidence is refused rather than stored.
A stored finding's first sighting is Potential; reproduction across scans is what makes it Confirmed.
Stored findings have a stable identity: the same flaw reported again updates its row and keeps the new severity.
Triage through the API refuses a suppression with no justification or one too short to be one, and records the decision in the audit log.
A resolved finding detected again becomes a regression, its disposition does not survive, and the stored scan's gate reads FAIL.
Security findings, scans and scopes are invisible to another tenant.
The platform's security gate and the JavaScript mirror produce the same decision and the same words; two implementations of one control do not drift.
A finding a scan could not reproduce goes to NeedsReview with the reason, and is never resolved on absence alone.
A finding reproduced after a scan missed it returns to Confirmed and the stale not-reproduced note is cleared.
A security trend carries the coverage each point was measured at, and flags a scan that covered materially less than the one before it.
An application with no recorded scan is described as untested, never as clean.

A security attack surface is derived from the knowledge graph: which endpoints take an object identifier, change state, take a file or carry a destination parameter, each naming the checks it implies.
An attack surface always carries the caveat that it describes what discovery walked rather than the application.
A change selects the security checks covering the surface it reaches, and a change matching nothing selects nothing rather than implying safety.
A narrowed security selection reports the full implied set as configured, so it cannot buy a passing gate.
A check covering a currently open finding stays selected whatever the change touched.
A release assessment always carries a security posture, and a build nobody scanned reads as NOT SECURITY TESTED rather than being omitted.
The platform and the engine name every security check identically.
A new Critical finding and a security regression each notify whoever is configured to care, at Problem severity, and neither message carries evidence, a payload or a response value.
